agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen word "stranger." The earlier cards give no way to reason out whether a stranger, servant or brother will enjoy the riches, so this is a wording guess rather than a test of meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The question begins "Say that man..." without identifying the man within the question. "That man" points back to earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: "That man" has no antecedent within the question. The question relies on earlier cards to identify the man being compared with the stillborn child instead of supplying that context itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Five of the stop's seven choice cards are multiple choice, and the other two are true or false. Multiple choice therefore dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

agent.problem: The setup only says that what the eye can see is better than "something else." It does not provide a picture or explanation from which to infer "the wandering of desire," leaving the baker to guess the next detail of the Teacher's line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

agent.problem: This card contains only a reaction joke about talking too much. It tells no new part of verse 11 and does not carry the passage forward toward verse 12.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

agent.problem: With only "few days" and "fleeting life" as setup, a shadow, a mist and a flower are all plausible pictures of brevity. Nothing in the earlier cards distinguishes the shadow, so the correct pick depends on luck or prior memory rather than reasoning.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
